newsitem.title: KENYA: Sudan rebels appoint deputy for eastern front.
newsitem.headline: Sudan rebels appoint deputy for eastern front.

text.p: Sudanese rebel military chief John Garang said on Wednesday a former Sudanese army officer was appointed his new deputy to step up rebel operations in eastern Sudan.
Garang, chairman of the joint military command for the rebel National Democratic Alliance (NDA), said former Lieutenant-General Abdulrahman Saed was appointed deputy chairman on June 30.
"He was deputy chief of staff before 1989 in the Sudanese army and is now deputy chairman of the joint military command," Garang told Reuters by telephone from Eritea's capital Asmara.

"This was done to envigorate the eastern front. We are doing a lot there. It is a very sensitive front. This sends a strong signal to the Sudanese army," said Garang, who heads the largest single rebel group, the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA).
He said the aim of rebel attacks in the northeast this year was to cut the road connecting the Red Sea port of Port Sudan to Khartoum, cutting off the capital from Sudan's only port.
In the south, he said rebels last Monday seized the White Nile River port of Shambe and were blocking barge supply traffic to the southern capital of Juba, 270 km (160 miles) to the south.
Juba, which has a large garrison, is still supplied by air.

He said in the southern provinces of Bahr al-Ghazal and Equatoria the Sudanese army controlled seven major garrisons including Juba but declined to say when rebels would move on the southern capital, which they have been slowly encircling.
The Sudanese government has accused Eritrean, Ethiopian and Ugandan troops of taking part in rebel offensives in the south, east and northeast since January. The three countries deny the charges.
The SPLA has fought since 1983 for independence or greater autonomy for the Christian and animist south from the Moslem and Arab north. The NDA says it wants to trigger an uprising in Khartoum.
